items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Chamblee Shamanie (PHONETIC), tenor player -- we all was raised in the same neighborhood somewhere

ctx.x: He said that you inspired him rather late?

I inspired him when Reverend Turner (PHONETIC) made that first old fiddle for me. Nevins and I were raised up in the same neighborhood, you know, on the South Side, at [unintelligible] and Ricards (PHONETIC), the trumpet player and Tommy "Madman" Jones (PHONETIC), Dinah Washington, who was Ruth Jones, when we knew her -- we all went to grade school -- went to Dolittle. Eddie Chamblee Shamanie (PHONETIC), tenor player -- we all was raised in the same neighborhood somewhere and Nevins and I used to run over to the…

He saw me one summer day after Reverend Turner made that fiddle, he was coming through the alley and I'm on the back porch playing with it and he said, "Let me play it." I said, "You think you can play it?" He said, "Yeah." He grabbed it and naturally he didn't know nothing about it. He was a beautiful person. So I took it from him. items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: working with Eddie Chamblee to the winter -- something happened between there and John Young.

ctx.x: Did Joe Joe have his show?

Well, what he called his Joe Joe Show, he'd have these little singers with him, and we played blues, shuffle blues arrangements, and they had people like Della Reese come in, Betty "Bebop" Bee-Bop Carter, two girls - all singers, you know, and that would be the show. That was in '53 on over gigging around different theaters, working with Eddie Chamblee to the winter -- something happened between there and John Young.

Then in '54, at the same time Ike Day died, I think that was in '54 when he passed away. In fact, that was when the doctor told him he had TB and told him if he didn't stop playing, it would kill him, and Ike said, "Well, I been playing all my life and that's the way I'm gonna die." And he almost did. It got so he would get on a bandstand, and on one session, you'd get him playing and his feet would swell up so bad, we'd have to help him up off the drums.
